introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.desc: An overview of the template architecture: a single entry, modular directories, and decoupled modules.
introduction.s1p: The root has one index.html entry; everything else follows the current project layout:
introduction.l1: app/core/ and app/components/ own the runtime, UI kit, and App Shell
introduction.l2: app/modules/ maps each top-level sidebar item to a business module
introduction.l3: app/styles/ keeps Nova design tokens and responsive styles in one place
introduction.l4: server/ provides the optional isomorphic Request → Response API
introduction.s2p: No runtime npm dependencies are required. Native ESM, Web Components, Shadow DOM, and a hand-written router form a deployable console.
introduction.s3p: Modules never import each other; each module works through core APIs, shared UI, and its own state.

getStarted.title: Get Started
getStarted.desc: Run Nova and add your first module in three steps.
getStarted.s1p: Use just dev to start the local Node server, or open index.html for the offline preview.
getStarted.s2p: Every top-level sidebar item is a module. Create its directory and declare the manifest:
getStarted.step2: Write module.config.js, index.js, components, and three locale files
getStarted.step3: Register a dynamic import in app/modules/registry.js and add server routes when the business needs them

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.desc: Notable capabilities in the migrated build.
changelog.l1: Preserves the template information architecture: Dashboard, Tasks, Apps, Chats, Docs, and Settings
changelog.l2: Rewrites pages and interactions with native Web Components, Shadow DOM, and Nova tokens
changelog.l3: Adds workspaces, profiles, collapsible sidebar, mobile drawer, and three languages
changelog.l4: Keeps zero runtime dependencies and the file:// offline preview
changelog.l5: All dialogs, selects, toasts, and empty states use the in-house UI components
